scopes.name: Restricted Adult Neurogenesis and Circuit Remodeling
scopes.scope: Adult neuron production and remodeling of existing circuits are distinct source-scoped processes. Selected mouse birth-label, electrophysiological and optogenetic assays support maturation and circuit participation in restricted dentate preparations; task, running, niche and injury effects concern separate stages and cohorts. Primate histology, human BrdU, radiocarbon models and transcript-based annotation have different inferential reach. Mature-spine remodeling need not entail neuron birth, normal adult neurogenesis need not follow injury, and no universal learning prerequisite, human cognitive mechanism or uniquely minimal construction rule is established.
unresolved: All existing assay-specific age, count, denominator, reporter, nesting, source-version, statistical and human sample-manifest uncertainties remain inherited; raw measurements and code are not independently reproduced by this scope reconstruction.

Distinguish generation, maturation, migration, survival, input, output, contact remodeling, replacement and behavior before any closed loop or construction rule. Longitudinal ancestry/contact identity, selective mediation and independent matched studies remain necessary.
Adult human functional integration and cognition, exact cross-species rates, complete birth/death balance, optimal remodeling and unique molecular/physical geometry remain unestablished.

scopes.name: Emotional and Affective Processing
scopes.scope: Affective processing is represented by projection-specific changes in mouse open-arm/center exploration under distinct BLA-to-CeA activation and inhibition preparations. Terminal activation and direct BLA somatic activation produce contrasting exploration outcomes; inhibition uses a separate low-stress bilateral preparation. These assays support bounded circuit effects on behavioral proxies. They do not measure subjective feeling, a single system-wide evaluative property or simultaneous control of valence, salience, cognition, perception, learning and motor readiness.
unresolved: Full supplemental controls, matched stress/laterality conditions, direct affective-outcome definitions, distributed readouts and separate cytokine/inflammation causal tests remain open.

scopes.name: Brain Oscillations and Rhythms
scopes.scope: Rhythmic organization is reconstructed through fast-spiking-cell activation that amplifies local gamma and a phase-sensitive whisker-response assay in barrel cortex. Local field potential, sorted unit response and stimulation timing remain distinct observables. The results support a preparation-bound intervention on temporal organization; they do not establish every frequency band, cross-frequency coupling, whole-brain synchrony, semantic code or universal prerequisite for cognition.
unresolved: Full main preparation and spectral methods, anesthetic state, endogenous versus driven rhythm, cross-area routing and competing nonoscillatory explanations require further tests.

scopes.name: Information Processing in Neural Connectomes
scopes.scope: Connectomic processing is reconstructed through targeted neural stimulation and downstream calcium responses in immobilized C. elegans. AVJR-to-AVDR and AVER-to-AVAR increases and a SAADL-to-OLLR decrease are preparation-bound effective responses, potentially including indirect routes. An anatomical connectome, a perturbation-response atlas, a statistical dependency and a Shannon communication model are distinct objects. The evidence does not identify every path, hub operation, recurrent computation, semantic content or a universal mapping from wiring to function.
unresolved: Direct versus indirect paths, response-classifier replay, full state/sampling sensitivity, explicit communication variables and held-out anatomy-to-function prediction remain open.

scopes.name: Emergence of Conscious Experience
scopes.scope: Conscious experience remains an explicitly unresolved theoretical scope. IIT, GNWT and conceptual global-workspace architecture are distinct versioned proposals, not one combined physiological rule. The COGITATE visual-task data provide region/feature/modality-dependent decoding, duration-related activity and differing preregistered phase versus exploratory amplitude connectivity results. These recordings neither causally generate experience nor measure Phi or establish a unique necessary integration threshold. Reportable access, neural content readout and subjective experience remain distinct explanatory targets.
unresolved: Theory-version reconciliation and correction notices, matched awareness/report contrasts, causal neural perturbations, held-out discrimination and an operational bridge to subjective experience remain open.

scopes.name: Cognitive Processing and Decision Making
scopes.scope: Decision making is reconstructed through task-specific macaque motion choices, reaction times, spatial free choices and perturbation time courses. LIP stimulation alters choices and response times, while one verified LIP-silencing design shows no detected motion deficit despite strong decision-related correlations; a different design reports early bias with attenuation. MT silencing and spatial control tasks give further contrasts. Evidence accumulation, competitive thresholds and compensation are candidate explanations, not a uniquely identified universal cognitive architecture.
unresolved: Task-matched perturbation comparisons, unbiased time-course analyses, selective mechanism tests and held-out model predictions are needed before a shared decision rule or general hierarchy.

scopes.name: Glial Regulation of Neural Activity
scopes.scope: Glial regulation is a family of source-specific interactions involving astrocytic ionic/uptake currents, lactate-related retention effects, myelin/conduction associations, developmental microglial engulfment, adult process responses and purinergic perturbations. These are not one homogeneous stabilizing property. Larval radial-astrocyte feedback and behavior oppose an absolute exclusion of glia from task-related information processing. Positive, negative and null outcomes retain cell class, age, region, manipulation and endpoint identity; no all-glia algorithm or universal regulatory architecture is admitted.
unresolved: Complete the already identified unread supporting methods and animal-level measurements before exact protocol or quantitative use; retain the Suzuki MCT2 rescue conflict, de Ceglia denominator conflict and Etxeberria text/caption discrepancies.
A unified ionic/metabolic/myelin/immune mechanism, long-term protection, cell-class transfer and whole-brain stability require matched endpoints and selective mediation tests.

scopes.name: Motor Coordination and Control
scopes.scope: Motor control is reconstructed through force-dependent hand-localization judgments, force-field reaching adaptation and field-removal aftereffects. The localization experiment contrasts assistive, resistive and null forces during constrained movement without arm vision; its tuned state-estimator account remains separate from the measured biases. Reaching adaptation supplies a different behavioral preparation with only abstract-level inherited reading. These examples do not identify one neural Kalman filter, all feedback/gain operations or a complete distributed movement-control circuit.
unresolved: Full force-field methods and participant identities, matched neural interventions, alternative estimator families, causal feedback pathways and cross-task stability bounds remain open.

scopes.name: Functional Specialization of Neural Ensembles
scopes.scope: Functional ensembles are reconstructed as operational calcium co-activation groups in a learned visual licking task. Nonselective stimulation can disrupt, and selected pattern-completion stimulation can improve, task-associated ensemble recruitment and measured performance, while non-pattern-completion controls do not show the same improvement. Gray-screen behavioral comparisons condition on a small successful-recall subset. These results support task- and selection-specific participation; they do not establish fixed anatomical modules, universal division of labor, minimum functional units or the subjective percept caused by stimulation.
unresolved: Raw trial and membership analyses, success-selection sensitivity, anatomical connectivity, separate-day controls, alternative ensemble definitions and selective cross-task necessity remain open.

scopes.name: Neural-State-Dependent Epigenetic and Transcriptional Modulation

scopes.name: Formation of Neural Networks
scopes.scope: Neural network formation is reconstructed through anatomical developmental comparisons in different C. elegans individuals and an axon-contact coculture intervention. Similar neurite geometry can coexist with changing chemical connectivity, while neuroligin-expressing nonneuronal contacts can induce local presynaptic differentiation. These are different species/preparations and different endpoints; neither establishes a complete persistent network, its physiological coupling weights, a universal modular architecture or a developmental hierarchy. scopes.name: Global Neurotransmitter Modulation
scopes.scope: Neuromodulation is reconstructed through optogenetic LC manipulations and EEG/EMG-defined mouse sleep/wake endpoints. Brief activation promotes awakening; prolonged active-period inhibition reduces wake duration but leaves awakenings possible; inactive-period inhibition has no detected duration effect. These schedule- and state-dependent results support a particular noradrenergic circuit contribution. scopes.name: Neurovascular Coupling
scopes.scope: The reconstructed vascular scope concerns activity-associated vascular responses, capillary potassium-sensitive signaling and arterial connexin-dependent response propagation. It separates isolated-cell current, ex vivo diameter/membrane potential, in vivo RBC flux, relative perfusion and optical HbT-related signals. Neural-to-vascular segments are experimentally constrained, but the physiological potassium source, segment transitions, full signal carrier and inverse neural readout remain unresolved. scopes.name: Placebo Responses and Psychosomatic Modulation
scopes.scope: Treatment descriptions, conditioning history and contextual procedures can change specific pain-tolerance, motor, hormone, immune-cell or symptom-report outcomes in existing participants. These endpoints have different mechanisms and controls: opioid-sensitive versus opioid-insensitive conditioned pain, nocebo slowing without proven positive motor gain, conditioned hormone/IL-2 changes with suggestion-only nulls, and perceived asthma relief without demonstrated sham bronchodilation. unresolved: Exact neural/autonomic mediation, durable set-point changes, long-term clinical outcomes and outcome-specific independent replication remain unestablished.

scopes.name: Sensory Integration and Perception
scopes.scope: Sensory integration is represented by a visual-haptic height-discrimination experiment in four adult observers. Manipulated visual reliability and small cue discrepancies alter combined judgments and thresholds in a way resembling a declared maximum-likelihood comparison. The model assumes aligned cues, independent Gaussian estimator noise and a uniform prior. This is bounded behavioral cue combination, not a directly identified neural implementation, every multisensory operation or proof of universally optimal or consciously unified perception.
unresolved: Correlated-noise, non-Gaussian and robust-integration alternatives, larger discrepancies, temporal alignment, developmental/generalization cohorts and neural necessity require separate tests.

scopes.name: Regulation of Sleep–Wake Cycles
scopes.scope: Sleep/wake regulation is reconstructed through EEG/EMG-defined mouse transition and duration endpoints under distinct Hcrt and LC interventions. Hcrt stimulation shortens post-stimulation wake latency under specified trains, with low-frequency and total-duration nulls and receptor-blockade contrasts. LC activation and inhibition have schedule- and circadian-period-dependent effects. Transition probability/latency, wake duration and sleep function are separate; two-process and synaptic-homeostasis accounts remain interpretations rather than experimentally closed universal state-control laws.
unresolved: Full supplemental data, latency exclusions, receptor-specific causal routes, homeostatic/circadian model equations and independent tests of consolidation, metabolic recovery and experience remain open.

scopes.name: Neural Mechanisms of Social Recognition and Empathy
scopes.scope: Social recognition, action observation, self-other distinction, affect sharing, mental-state attribution and helping are distinct constructs and outcomes. Macaque F5 recordings, clinical human action units, cued partner-pain fMRI and clinical pain-picture iEEG/ratings support their own sampled responses, not one necessary mirror/empathy circuit. Proposed shared representations and shared-manifold/neurodynamic mechanisms remain hypotheses, with instrument identity, spatial-overlap, statistical-directionality and clinical-sampling boundaries explicit.
unresolved: Primary recognition/agency/helping interventions, selective circuit tests, matched nonpain aversive comparisons and participant-disjoint decoder transfer remain open.

scopes.name: Neural Mechanisms of Symbolic Representation
scopes.scope: Symbolic representation is a family of operational definitions and hypotheses concerning reference, composition, transfer and internal use beyond a present stimulus. Sequence continuation, eye movements, fMRI/MEG and neural-network embedding analyses provide distinct bounded tests; they do not jointly demonstrate a complete neural language of thought or one necessary physical construction. Fixed-language description costs, proposed vector binding, program induction and conceptual bootstrapping remain separate from measured circuits, universal minimum resources and a general-purpose stable cognitive capacity.
unresolved: Universal symbolic faculty, the neural implementation of compositional binding and true held-out construction/generalization remain unestablished.
Existing primary/source-code reading limits, syntax/count/coordinate conflicts and unchanged deposited-readout checks remain attached to their original records; no new replay is claimed.

scopes.name: Synaptic Plasticity and Learning
scopes.scope: Activity-dependent plasticity is represented by persistent dentate population-response changes after perforant-path conditioning and NMDA-antagonist sensitivity of CA1 potentiation induction. Behavioral force-field adaptation and aftereffects provide a separate learning-related trajectory, without a directly measured bridge to those hippocampal synapses. Potentiation induction, basal transmission, excitability, behavioral retention and structural remodeling are not interchangeable. The general claim that synaptic history implements learning remains a hypothesis requiring task-specific causal tests.
unresolved: Read full original hippocampal methods and test specific storage mechanisms in matched behavioral tasks; LTD, structural remodeling, general retention and transfer remain outside these assays.

scopes.name: Network Synchronization and Criticality
scopes.scope: Collective dynamics are reconstructed through sampled LFP event cascades in cortical cultures, separate drug-activated acute slices and the distributional response to culture picrotoxin. Event threshold, sampling and binning define an avalanche; phase synchronization and criticality at a specified transition require additional observables. Recovery of an event-size distribution after washout supports a bounded reversible perturbation. Scale-like statistics alone do not prove self-organized criticality, optimal information processing or a necessary organizational condition for cognition.
unresolved: Raw event/bin sensitivity, transition-specific order parameters, alternative-model tests, the unresolved Figure 4 refractory discrepancy and independent biological performance measurements remain open.

scopes.name: Thalamic Visual Relay and Gain Control
scopes.scope: Thalamic visual transfer is reconstructed through paired-spike retinal efficacy and separate corticogeniculate perturbation results. Closely spaced retinal spikes differ in conditional transfer efficacy; removing layer-6 cortical input can increase or decrease dLGN responses depending on cell and contrast, while driving input reduces evoked counts in the read source. The feedback preparation uses adult GN220 Ntsr1-Cre mice during acute isoflurane-anesthetized recordings, with concentration adjusted around 1.2% using cortical LFP state. These observations distinguish retinal transmission from cortical feedback and exclude one universal positive-gain sign. They do not identify the transfer's unique cellular mechanism or jointly establish awake attention, neuromodulation, noise suppression and oscillatory routing.
unresolved: Remaining corticogeniculate methods and raw data, matched awake-state experiments, transfer mechanism, neuromodulatory interactions, attention and noise/phase-control outcomes require additional primary evidence.

scopes.name: Predictive and Top-Down Modulation of Visual Attention
scopes.scope: Top-down visual modulation is reconstructed through sub-saccadic-threshold FEF stimulation and V4 response changes, complemented by a separate corticogeniculate feedback assay. Retinotopically corresponding FEF stimulation enhances responses while noncorresponding stimulation can suppress them, with dependence on stimulus configuration. This supports a bounded intervention on visual response gain. Predictive coding, expectation comparison, error signals and iterative internal-world-model control remain explicit interpretations requiring task-matched alternatives; top-down modulation and prediction are not synonymous measurements.
unresolved: Full FEF methods and exact species/preparation, matched expectation-versus-attention manipulations, prediction-error observables, causal routes and held-out competing-model tests remain open.

scopes.name: Primary Visual Cortex Feature Maps
scopes.scope: Visual feature organization is reconstructed through a primate striate-cortex column report, rat V1 orientation selectivity without discernible local orientation organization and a separate cat area-18 comparison. Feature selectivity and spatial maps are distinct; a selective population need not display a locally ordered map at the sampled scale. Functionally assigned thalamocortical connections favor matching contrast sign and receptive-field alignment, but correlation-based assignment does not establish map development. The original 1962 cat reference and 1968 monkey study retain their distinct identities.
unresolved: Complete historical methods, developmental perturbations, spatial-scale sensitivity, direct anatomical matching and causal downstream form-processing tests remain open.

scopes.scope: Working memory is represented by specified delayed-task maintenance and interference/priority readouts, with storage, rehearsal, binding, control and updating as distinct functional constructs. Macaque PF recordings and human fMRI/TMS-EEG/behavior contexts support bounded observations without identifying a unique continuous-firing or silent-synaptic mechanism. Guided activation, episodic buffering and adaptive gating remain attributed proposals. A process classification does not establish a complete executive architecture, universal time window or mandatory cognitive-control/plasticity/rhythm construction chain.
